title: Rabbi Chiyya of Avel Arav
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Pesachim 72a: “But did not Rabbi Chiyya of Avel Arav teach: Rabbi Meir said,” and the gloss attributed to Rashi explains that it is a place-name. Hyman argues that this is not from Rashi because it is enclosed in brackets: []. Hyman notes that in the statement in Shabbat 137a the words “of Avel Arav” are absent, and likewise they are absent in Dikdukei Soferim. Our master the Ittur, Hilkhot Milah, cites that the reading should be “Meir erev” — a mnemonic that Rabbi Meir stated the law that Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree concerning one who had two infants to circumcise, one on the eve (erev) of Shabbat. Hyman explains that since there at 72b it reads “Rabbi Shimon said: They did not disagree,” etc., they placed a mnemonic that here Rabbi Meir said so; but in Shabbat 137a the mnemonic is absent, for there this mnemonic does not apply.

notes.text: The bracket-based Rashi attribution argument and Meir/erev mnemonic are Hyman’s proposals. Saved Davidson Pesachim72a actually includes bracketed מאבל ערב and fully writes Eliezer and Yehoshua. Digital brackets are not independent proof of printed correction history.

The consulted Pesachim 72a contains the bracketed words “of Avel Arav” and explicitly names Eliezer and Yehoshua. Those digital brackets do not prove Hyman’s claim about Rashi’s authorship or a printed correction history. The Ittur mnemonic and exact Dikdukei Soferim omission remain reports by Hyman, not independently inspected edition findings.
